description: Norwegian Prescription Database (NorPD) The Norwegian Prescription Database is a nationwide register that records every prescription drug dispensed by community pharmacies in Norway — including prescriptions for individuals, institutions (hospitals, nursing homes) and even veterinary use — from 1 January 2004 onward【3†L1-L5】【4†L1-L4】. It captures the patient’s unique identifier, age, sex, geographic region, dispensing date, drug name, ATC code, strength, quantity and prescriber information. The database was established and is maintained by the Norwegian Institute of Public Health (Folkehelseinstituttet, FHI), which operates it under national health‑register legislation【2†L1-L4】. Purpose & typical use cases NorPD was created to monitor national drug utilisation, support pharmaco‑epidemiological research, evaluate prescribing quality and safety, and inform public‑health policy. Researchers have used it to study drug adherence, opioid misuse, disease risk (e.g., Parkinson’s disease), and the impact of policy changes on medication use. Key features / unique aspects - Near‑complete coverage: ~5.8 million individuals (≈ 99 % of the population) and >620 million dispensed medication records have been captured to date【2†L1-L3】. - Individual‑level linkage: each record can be stratified by sex, age, and geography, enabling fine‑grained analyses. - Inclusion of institutional dispensing (hospitals, nursing homes) and veterinary prescriptions, which many other national drug registers lack. - Open‑access statistical extracts are available through the Norwegian data portal, while detailed individual‑level data require approved research applications. Overall, NorPD is a unique, high‑resolution resource for drug‑utilisation surveillance and health‑services research in Norway.
